introduction.p: Let f(x)={3x^{2}+x+5} and let T_2(x)=b_0+b_1x+b_2x^2\text{.} We find the values of b_0, b_1 and b_2 that make the functions f(x) and T_2(x) have the same height, slope, and concavity at x=0\text{.}

statement.p: Complete the table below by computing derivatives of T_2(x) and {3x^{2}+x+5} and evaluating them at x=0 as directed.
Now, since we want T_2(x) and {3x^{2}+x+5} to have the same height at x=0\text{,} set T_2(0)=f(0)\text{.}
Since we want T_2(x) and {3x^{2}+x+5} to have the same slope at x=0\text{,} set T_2'(0)=f'(0)\text{.}
Finally, since we want T_2(x) and {3x^{2}+x+5} to have the same concavity at x=0\text{,} set T_2''(0)=f''(0)\text{.}
Putting everything together, what is the resulting formula for T_2(x)=b_0+b_1x+b_2x^2\text{?}
What does your answer mean about the quadratic approximation to a quadratic function?
